safety_verdicts.content: The headache improves when the patient is lying down.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies improvement when lying down, but the generated facts do not explicitly state improvement with lying down (only 'no postural worsening').
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting that the headache improves when lying down helps characterize a possible orthostatic/postural component (e.g., CSF leak-type pattern) and can meaningfully alter the differential and advice. Omitting this detail could reduce diagnostic accuracy and lead to less appropriate follow-up guidance if symptoms persist.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating “no red flag features” while including “no thunderclap onset” without explicit assessment/documentation can create false reassurance and may reduce urgency of escalation in subsequent reviews, particularly because thunderclap onset is a critical red flag for subarachnoid hemorrhage. This is higher-risk than routine documentation noise because it asserts absence of a dangerous feature that was not clearly established.
